title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 3rd version, June 1986). M is a poset of 'lieux' with inclusion ≤. A second relation ≪ is the 'shadow' (ombre) relation. Z ≪ X is best read as 'Z lies in the shadow/closure of X'. Z °≪ X is an 'interior' strengthening. Λ ⊂ M is a dense family of small lieux, playing the role of points or germs. Notation: omb_Λ(X) = {Z ∈ Λ : Z ≪ X}, Omb(X) = {Z ∈ M : Z ≪ X}, and X̃ = {X' ∈ M : X' ≤ X}. There is also a compatibility relation, written with a crossed symbol (rendered here ≬ / ⋈ / ∦), between pairs of lieux.

The page states a Proposition listing the 'characteristic properties' of a system (M, ≤, ≪, ≬, Λ ⊂ M) arising from a shadow relation with Λ dense:

- MΛ0 ('trivial axiom'): X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪ Y.
- MΛ1 ('refinements on the right'): if Y ≪ X, X' ≤ X, Z ∈ Λ and Z ≪ Y, Z ≪ X', then there is Y' ≤ Y with Y' ≪ X' and Z ≪ Y'. In set form: omb_Λ(Y) ∩ omb_Λ(X') = ∪_{Y' ≤ Y, Y' ≪ X'} omb_Λ(Y'). He hesitates over notation for the index set. When Y ≤ X the index set can be taken as Ỹ ∩ X̃'.
- MΛ2 (density of Λ): every X contains some Z ∈ Λ with Z °≪ X.
- MΛ3 ('minimal interior'): if Z ∈ Λ and Z ≪ X, then some X' ≤ X has Z °≪ X'.
- MΛ4 (saturation): ≬ is reflexive, symmetric and decreasing, i.e. X ≬ Y, X' ≤ X, Y' ≤ Y ⇒ X' ≬ Y'.
- MΛ5: if X ≬ Y and Z ∈ Λ with Z ≪ X, Z ≪ Y, then there is Z' with Z ≪ Z' ≤ X, Y. In set form: omb_Λ(X) ∩ omb_Λ(Y) = ∪_{Z' ∈ X̃ ∩ Ỹ} omb_Λ(Z').

He notes that only MΛ4 and MΛ5 involve ≬. He then introduces an intrinsic relation R, defined from (M, ≤, ≪) alone: R(X,Y) ⇔ for every Z ∈ M with Z ≪ X, Z ≪ Y there is Z' with Z ≪ Z' ≤ X, Y. Equivalently Omb(X) ∩ Omb(Y) = ∪_{Z' ≤ X, Y} Omb(Z').

Geometric meaning: if ≪ is 'contained in the closure', R(X,Y) says the shadows (closures) of X and Y meet only along shadows of common sub-lieux. This is a 'good intersection' or frontier-type condition. It fails for badly placed tame sets, e.g. two semi-algebraic cells whose closures touch at a point not in the closure of any common piece.

Purpose: the next page shows R is hereditary under ≤ (using MΛ1). Hence MΛ5 becomes 'X ≬ Y ⇒ R(X,Y)', so the admissible compatibility relations are exactly the reflexive, symmetric, decreasing sub-relations of R, with R the largest. Equality ≬ = R holds only in special cases. He then aims to recover ≬ from its restriction to Λ. Overall this is a point-free, order-theoretic axiomatization of the 'shadow/closure' structure behind a tame topology of lieux. It serves the earlier lemmas (p. 30, Lemma A', Lemma B), which need the intersection formula for shadows.
errors: MΛ5 quantifies only over Z ∈ Λ (shadows omb_Λ), whereas R quantifies over all Z ∈ M (Omb). 'X ≬ Y ⇒ R(X,Y)' (stated on the next page) does not follow from MΛ5 as written. For Z ∈ M one gets, for each Λ-element in the shadow of Z, some Z' ≤ X, Y, but not a single Z' with Z ≪ Z'. Bridging this needs an extra argument or axiom; the margin of p. 41 ('on peut se borner au cas Z∈Λ') asserts but does not prove it.

The displayed set equalities in MΛ1 and MΛ5 implicitly use transitivity-type properties of ≪ (Z ≪ Y' ≤ Y ⇒ Z ≪ Y, and Z ≪ Y' ≪ X' ⇒ Z ≪ X'). These are not listed among MΛ0–MΛ5 on this page; presumably they are standing axioms of the shadow relation from earlier pages.
The index set in the MΛ1 union is left unsettled (crossed-out 'Ỹ ∩ Omb(X')' with 'quelle notation'). The variant with Ỹ ∩ X̃' when Y ≤ X is stated without justification.

ideas.what: Point-free axiomatics of a 'shadow' (closure/adherence) relation ≪ on a poset of lieux with a dense subfamily Λ (axioms MΛ0–MΛ3)
ideas.modern_name: closest analogues: proximity/'well-inside' relations, Wallman-type lattice bases, abstract closure/incidence structures on posets of cells
ideas.usually_credited_to: proximity spaces: Efremovich (1950s), de Vries (1962); Wallman (1938) for lattice-based spaces; nothing specific for tame-topology lieux
ideas.where_published: Only the general wish for a tame topology appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (1984); this axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Compatibility relation ≬ between lieux, required to be reflexive, symmetric, decreasing, and to satisfy the shadow-intersection formula omb(X)∩omb(Y) = ∪_{Z'≤X,Y} omb(Z')
ideas.modern_name: frontier/regular-intersection condition (closure of intersection controls intersection of closures), as in compatibility of cells with a stratification satisfying the frontier condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: frontier condition in stratification theory: Whitney, Thom, Mather; cell decomposition compatibility in o-minimality: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn

ideas.what: Intrinsic maximal compatibility relation R defined from (M, ≤, ≪) alone; admissible ≬ are exactly the hereditary reflexive-symmetric sub-relations of R
ideas.modern_name: largest hereditary relation satisfying the intersection-of-closures condition (a 'well-intersecting pairs' relation)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic, order-theoretic (point-free) framework for tame topology. It is built on a poset of lieux, a shadow/closure relation, a dense family of 'point-like' lieux, and a compatibility relation. He isolates an intrinsic maximal compatibility relation R expressing that closures meet only along closures of common sub-lieux. The framework is left at the axiom-listing stage, and the reduction from Λ-quantification to M-quantification is unproved.
missed.quote: Notons R la relation (définie en termes de (M, ≤, ≪) seulement ...): R(X,Y) ⟺ ∀Z∈M avec Z≪X, Z≪Y, ∃Z'∈M avec Z≪Z'≤X,Y i.e. Omb(X)∩Omb(Y)=⋃_{Z'∈X̃∩Ỹ}Omb(Z')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Abstract, point-free approaches to tame/o-minimal topology and to stratifications with the frontier condition remain sparse. This gives a concrete candidate axiom set, with a natural maximal 'good-intersection' relation, that could be compared to definable cell decompositions or to locale-theoretic treatments. The value is mainly historical, documenting what Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' was meant to look like.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, fairly original axiomatization belonging to Grothendieck's tame-topology project, of which little detail is in print. Mathematically, however, it is preliminary bookkeeping (axiom lists plus a maximal relation) rather than a striking result.
transcription_corrections: Header likely reads 'provenant d'une relation ombre avec Λ dense dans M' (a 'shadow relation with Λ dense'); the '[?]' marks are probably unnecessary.
The compatibility symbol is a crossed/X-shaped relation sign (as on p. 41, rendered there as ∦ or 'not ⊥'). It should be rendered consistently rather than as ⋈ in some places and ≭ elsewhere.
MΛ1 hypothesis: in the image a ≥ sign under X points to X' (X ≥ X'), consistent with the transcription; Z ∈ Λ is underlined with a wavy line.

The text below the axioms reads approximately: 'Ce sont deux axiomes seulement qui font intervenir X ≬ Y. L'axiome MΛ4 est un axiome de saturation. Pour MΛ5, notons R la relation (définie en termes de (M, ≤, ≪) seulement, sans y faire intervenir Λ ni ≬)'.

Margin labels are approximately: 'Axiome trivial' (MΛ0); 'Axiome des affinements à droite' (MΛ1); 'Axiome de densité de Λ' (MΛ2); 'Axiome de l'intérieur minimal' (MΛ3). A boxed margin note near MΛ1 appears to refer to MΛ4 and MΛ5.
In MΛ2 and MΛ3 the relation is the interior shadow Z °≪ X (≪ with a small circle), not Z °< X.
